policy_actions.l: Agricultural land use — agricultural land area (% total)
policy_actions.p: Preventive investment — gross capital formation (% GDP)

notes.investment: Gross capital formation captures all investment including fossil infrastructure, explaining positive CO2 coefficients in some countries. A consistent climate-specific investment indicator is unavailable across all countries in World Bank data.
notes.methane: Total methane excluding LULUCF is used to avoid conceptual overlap with the agricultural land variable and to maintain cross-sector coverage.
notes.small_countries: Countries with fewer than 20 clean observations are excluded from Level 1 estimation. Their pooled FE elasticities serve as fallback values in the RL environment.
notes.france_renewables: France exhibits a positive renewables elasticity (0.140, ns) because approximately 70-75% of electricity is nuclear. Renewable additions displace nuclear rather than fossil fuels, producing no measurable CO2 reduction. Consistent with IEA France energy profiles.
notes.estonia_renewables: Estonia exhibits a positive renewables elasticity (0.337, p<0.05) reflecting its historical dependence on oil shale for electricity. During the sample period, renewable expansion coincided with growing industrial output, producing a positive correlation between renewable share and total emissions. This is a structural feature of the Estonian economy, not an estimation error.
notes.norway_renewables: Norway exhibits the largest negative renewables elasticity (-1.221, p<0.01) because approximately 90% of electricity is hydropower. Additional renewable capacity directly displaces fossil fuel use in heating and industry.
notes.switzerland_agriland: Switzerland exhibits an extreme AgriLand elasticity (8.574) that is likely driven by multicollinearity or very low variation in agricultural land share (~10% of territory). Small absolute changes in land area produce large percentage changes in the log-log specification. This coefficient is flagged as unreliable. Switzerland is retained in the model for pooled estimation but its AgriLand elasticity should not be used for policy inference. The pooled FE estimate serves as fallback.
notes.pooled_vs_country_heterogeneity: The pooled FE renewables elasticity is positive (+0.026) while the country-specific OLS mean is negative (-0.181). This divergence occurs because expanding to 29 countries introduces Eastern European economies with high fossil dependency where renewables expansion historically coincided with economic growth. The pooled model masks this heterogeneity. Country-specific estimates remain economically interpretable and are the appropriate inputs for heterogeneous RL agents. This result strengthens the case for the hierarchical approach over a single pooled specification.
notes.non_significant_coefficients: Many country-level coefficients are not statistically significant (p > 0.10). This is expected given the limited time series per country (20-32 observations) and the number of regressors. Non-significant coefficients are retained in the model — they represent the best available point estimate for each country given the available data. The pooled FE estimates serve as a more statistically stable benchmark.
notes.extreme_coefficients: Countries with any coefficient exceeding |5.0| in absolute value are flagged in the output. These likely reflect multicollinearity, very low baseline variable variation, or influential outliers in the country-specific time series.

e.interpretation: At maximum effort, Renewables changes by +0.800 % share per period.

m.interpretation: At maximum effort, Methane changes by -0.201 MtCO2eq per period.

l.interpretation: At maximum effort, AgriLand changes by -0.248 % land area per period.

p.interpretation: At maximum effort, Investment changes by +1.045 % GDP per period.

budget_constraints.interpretation: An agent is allocated a total effort budget of 1.0 per period. Each lever consumes a fraction of this budget proportional to its estimated relative cost. An agent cannot set all levers to maximum simultaneously without exceeding the budget.
budget_constraints.cost_derivation: Proxy estimates derived from first-difference panel regressions of ln(Investment) on changes in each lever variable. These capture statistical association between lever changes and investment pressure, not causal costs. Coefficients are normalised to sum to 1.0.

Renewables_to_Investment.description: Renewable expansion historically associated with higher capital investment

Investment_to_GDP_PC.description: Investment level influences economic output per capita

GDP_PC_to_EnergyPC.description: Economic output per capita is a structural driver of energy demand

state_transition.specification: log-log elasticity model with country-specific intercepts
state_transition.time_step: One simulation step corresponds to one calendar year.
state_transition.trend_definition: trend(t) = year(t) - mean(years_in_sample). For the 1990-2021 sample, mean year ≈ 2005.5. At t=2021: trend = 15.5. Increment by 1 each period.

transition_function.step_1_action_to_delta: delta_X = action_mappings[country][action][level]  (signed: negative for decrease levers, positive for increase levers)
transition_function.step_3_clip_state: X(t+1) = clip(X(t+1), lower_bound, upper_bound) — see state_constraints for bounds
transition_function.step_5_co2_prediction: ln_CO2(t+1) = intercept[country] + elasticity_e * ln_Renewables(t+1) + elasticity_m * ln_Methane(t+1) + elasticity_l * ln_AgriLand(t+1) + elasticity_p * ln_Investment(t+1) + beta_GDP_PC * ln_GDP_PC(t+1) + beta_EnergyPC * ln_EnergyPC(t+1) + beta_Industry * ln_Industry(t+1) + beta_Urban * ln_Urban(t+1) + beta_trend * trend(t+1)

state_transition.elasticity_source: Use country_elasticities[country] for policy lever and control elasticities. Use pooled_fe_elasticities as fallback if country is not available.
state_transition.control_evolution: GDP_PC, EnergyPC, Industry, Urban are slowly evolving structural variables. They may be held constant or updated via constraint_relationships.
state_transition.budget_enforcement: Before applying actions, verify: sum(relative_costs[action] * normalised_effort[action]) <= total_budget. Reject or clip infeasible action combinations.
state_transition.reward_signal: CO2(t+1) is the environmental consequence output of this model. The reward function is defined within the RL environment and may incorporate CO2 reduction targets, economic costs, and cooperation terms.
